main_text.p: Verstegan. Restitut. cap. 1. & Voss. in voce Saxa.

Scefti, vel fcepfti, fagittæ] Hæc Sax. rcefrar, nobis hodie shafts, forte à thave, Teut. schaben, tondere, radere, ut Sagittæ radi solent ab Arcuariis: nisi à sceaf malis, i, e. Fascis: quòd sagittæ in fasces solent colligari, unde nobis a theaf of arrowes.
Scepeno, Judex: hodie scepenen, scabini] De hoc plura apud sæpius laudat. Lindenbrog. & Voss.
Sceithlon, Verticem, & scetlon] Scýtehealo Sax, præceps, item oblì-quus.
Scerns, Subsannatio; & scern, illu-sio] scorne nobis, eodem sensu.

Sclert, Lucidum] Limpidus, clarus, nobis sheere, & shire, unde aqua ejus-modi, nobis sheer (vel shire) water. Hinc oppidi & castri apud Dorseten-ses nostros, Shirborne dicti, nominis origo: quòd scil. ad Fontem limpidum situm sit. Cambden.
Sctimo, Splendor: nos schijne] Angli similiter; voce ortâ à Sax. rciman, splendere, fulgere.
Scieumo, Citò] Nobis to fkime, eo-dem

page.notes: Marginal handwritten number "242" in the right margin is not printed and is omitted. Several Old English words are set in black letter and rendered as printed; doubtful letters are not marked, the page is low resolution.
